version.changelog:
quickintel-scan v1.0.4

- Added a "Security Model" section to the documentation, clearly outlining the trust boundaries and confirming the service is strictly read-only.
- Clarified user responsibilities—emphasized never sharing private keys and treating results as informational, not guarantees.
- Provided explicit verification steps for users to independently validate scan results.
- Listed operator information, usage context, and third-party integrations for increased transparency.
- No changes to endpoints, triggers, costs, or API parameters.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (calling Quick Intel's read-only scan API and handling a small x402 payment) matches its instructions and required surface: it asks for no credentials, has no install step, and explicitly warns not to share private keys.

dimensions.detail: The name/description describe a token security scanner and the SKILL.md consistently documents calling Quick Intel's scan endpoint and the x402 payment flow. There are no unrelated requested binaries, environment variables, or config paths that would be inconsistent with a read-only scan service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions restrict inputs to a token contract address and chain and describe the HTTP 402/x402 payment flow. The document explicitly instructs users not to paste private keys and states Quick Intel is read-only. The instructions do not ask the agent to read local files, environment secrets, or other unrelated system state.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files — this is instruction-only, so nothing is written to disk or installed by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. It does require a wallet-based payment signature in order to pay $0.03 USDC per scan, which is proportional to the paid API model described and does not imply the skill needs private keys or broad credential access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request any persistent system privileges or modifications to other skills/config. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but is not combined with elevated privileges or secret access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent, but take basic precautions before use: 1) Never paste private keys or seed phrases into prompts — if the agent asks for them, stop. 2) The flow requires a wallet signature to pay $0.03 USDC; confirm the payment request through your wallet UI (check recipient domain/address and amount) and prefer hardware or well-known wallet apps when signing. 3) Independently verify the endpoint/domain (x402.quickintel.io) and the company (quickintel.io) before sending payments. 4) Treat scan results as one data point—cross-check on block explorers and DEXs for large trades. 5) If you need stronger assurance, test with a single low-cost scan first and verify the network/TLS details in your wallet/payment UI.
